prompt: In a $30°$-$60°$-$90°$ triangle, the side opposite the $30°$ angle has length $5$. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
hint: The sides are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$, shortest opposite the $30°$.

hints.text: The sides are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$, shortest opposite the $30°$.
The hypotenuse is twice the shortest side.

explanation: In a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle the sides are $x$, $x\sqrt{3}$, and $2x$, with $x$ opposite the $30°$ angle.
The remaining side, opposite the $60°$, is $5\sqrt{3}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Bigger angle, bigger opposite side
steps: In any triangle the largest angle faces the longest side.
So the $30°$ faces the shortest side and the $90°$ faces the hypotenuse — this orders the sides without memorizing which is which.
If your answer puts a long side opposite a small angle, you have matched them backwards.
